title: probe-farm-orchestration-for-rare-regressions-2026
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Design and operational playbook for the Probe Farm: an orchestration layer that runs targeted synthetic and production-derived probes to detect rare regressions and degradation in model quality across deployments (hosted, dedicated, private).
overview: This document describes the Probe Farm architecture, workflows, and operational rules used by Applied ML and Evals to catch low-frequency and long-tail regressions before they reach customers. The Probe Farm combines synthetic honeypots, stratified traffic probes, and workload fingerprints to prioritize probes, triage signals, and automate remediation paths (alerting, shadow rollbacks, or escalation).
motivation: High-volume and heterogeneous workloads can mask rare failures. Traditional slice-based evals miss low-occurrence regressions that nevertheless have outsized customer impact. The Probe Farm provides continuous, prioritized probing with automated fault classification and escalation to reduce mean-time-to-detection for these events.
scope: Covers design and runbook for: probe generation, scheduling, orchestration with shadow/canary paths, scoring heuristics, alert thresholds, minimal remediation actions, and ownership. Not in scope: core serving runtime optimizations (see eng-serving-runtime/runbooks) and enterprise legal compliance guidance.
definitions: Probe: a single request or small batch designed to exercise a targeted behavioral slice. Probe Farm: orchestration system that manages probe lifecycle and analysis. Honeypot: synthetic probe intentionally crafted to expose regressions. Fingerprint: compact workload metadata (token distribution, average seq len, function-call usage) used to route probes.
architecture_diagram: Text diagram: (Probe Producer) -> (Probe Scheduler) -> [Router: live-shadow | canary | production-mirror] -> (Serving Fleet) -> (Analyzer) -> (Signal Gateway -> Alerting / Rollback / Triage Queue). Fingerprints live in the Probe Catalog and inform scheduler priorities.
probe_farm_design:
Key components and responsibilities:
- Probe Producer: generates probes from three sources: synthetic honeypots, replayed rare slices from shadow traces, and stratified live sampling.
- Probe Catalog: metadata store for probes including fingerprint tags, labels, expected assertions, and historical outcomes.
- Scheduler: prioritizes probes using risk score (impact x uncertainty) and enforces rate limits per model/route.
- Router: decides execution path (immediate canary, shadow, or traffic-mirror) based on customer tier and SLOs.
- Analyzer: runs deterministic checks, semantic diffing, and ML-based anomaly classifiers.
- Signal Gateway: deduplicates signals, attaches provenance, and emits alerts to PagerDuty/Slack or to the regression triage queue.
orchestration_workflow:
Operational workflow (numbered):
1) Ingest: new probe seed arrives from dataset curators, production telemetry, or synthetic generator.
2) Fingerprint Matching: compute fingerprint and match to active route/model tags.
3) Risk Scoring: compute risk = impact_score * uncertainty_score. Impact_score derived from customer exposure and SLA; uncertainty_score from historical variance.
4) Schedule: if risk > high_threshold (0.8), schedule for immediate canary shadow; if 0.4 < risk <= 0.8, run as prioritized shadow; otherwise run in background probe queue.
5) Execute: router dispatches the probe. For canary probes, a fast-path small-percent traffic mirror is used; for shadow probes, responses are captured but not surfaced to end users.
6) Analyze: Analyzer applies assertion checks (exact-match, embedding-similarity, function-call validation) and ML anomaly detection.
7) Signal: if analyzer fires, Signal Gateway deduplicates and enriches with probe metadata and triage hints.
8) Response: automated remediation if confidence high (e.g., revert canary, scale up quantized variant), else create incident in regression triage with owner assignment.
evaluation_heuristics:
Heuristics and checks used by Analyzer:
- Deterministic assertions: token-level changes for exact behavior probes (threshold: > 15% token diffs flagged).
- Semantic similarity: cosine(embedding(a), embedding(b)) < 0.78 triggers semantic alert for open-ended outputs.
- Function-call validation: missing or malformed function-call when previously present -> immediate high-severity signal.
- Latency-correlated failures: increase in 95p latency aligned with quality degradation marks mixed-failure class.
- Ensemble voting: combine n=3 variant responses; if majority disagrees with baseline and confidence > 0.6, escalate.
- Temporal drift detector: rolling-window KL divergence on token-distribution; > 0.12 over 24h triggers slice creation for further evaluation.
metrics_and_alerting:
Primary metrics and alert thresholds:
- Detection latency (time from probe execution to actionable alert): SLO = 2h, threshold alert at 4h.
- Precision of automated remediation decisions: target >= 0.72.
- False positive rate on probes that create incidents: target <= 0.12.
- Probe coverage: percent of active workload fingerprints exercised weekly: target >= 85%.
- Regression recurrence rate (same signature re-detected within 7d): goal <= 0.05.
Alert routing: PagerDuty for sev>=2, Slack #regression-alerts with brief triage card for sev 3, email digest for low severity. Alerts include: probe id, fingerprint, risk score, diffs, and suggested remediation steps.
rollout_and_safety:
Safe rollout and automation guardrails:
- Automation gate: only allow automatic rollbacks or model swaps when Analyzer confidence >= 0.92 and historical remediation precision for that probe-type >= 0.80.
- Canary limits: max 0.5% traffic mirrored for a canary probe unless explicit approval.
- Quota enforcement: per-customer and per-model probe rates to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
- Human-in-the-loop: any probe that affects customer-observed outputs triggers a mandatory on-call notification and 15-minute hold for automated remediation to allow manual abort.
- Audit: all automated actions logged with trace ids and stored for 180 days in compliance with platform retention policies.
ownership_and_escalation:
Ownership matrix:
- Probe Farm platform: Applied ML (evals) team (primary), SRE (support).
- Analyzer model maintenance: Applied ML Research (primary), Eng-Serving-Runtime (consult).
- Incident triage and remediation: Model Owner (primary), Customer Success (notification).
Escalation paths:
- Sev 1/2: immediate PagerDuty page to on-call model owner and SRE lead.
- Repeated false positives (>3 within 7d): open a review with Applied ML and Product to tune probe heuristics.
config_table:
Recommended probe config fields (CSV-style rows):
name,fingerprint_tags,execution_path,rate_limit_per_min,assertions,remediation_policy
honeypot-rare-names,[ner,person,lowfreq],shadow,2,semantic-sim<0.78|funccall-present,revert-to-stable
synthetic-code-instrument,[code,func-call],canary,0.1,funccall-structure|exact-sig,redeploy-previous
replay-stratified-edge,[long-context,kv-cache-heavy],background,5,embedding-sim<0.75,create-triage
Notes: rate_limit_per_min uses fractional values to indicate percent of traffic for canaries (0.1 = 0.1% of route).
cli_examples:
Example probe lifecycle commands:
# create a new probe seed from a JSON file
rw-probe create --file probes/honeypot-rare-names.json --priority high
# schedule an immediate canary run against model v2.4
rw-probe run --id PF-2026-001 --model redwood-gpt-2.4 --path canary --max-traffic 0.2
# fetch probe results and analysis
rw-probe status --id PF-2026-001 --json > /tmp/pf-001-result.json
# promote probe result into triage
rw-probe triage --id PF-2026-001 --owner-team applied-ml --ticket SUMMARY-123
playbook_steps_for_oncall:
Oncall quick runbook (numbered):
1) Receive alert with probe id and severity.
2) Open analysis panel link and validate provenance (probe catalog entry, execution path).
3) If automation already remediated, verify customer impact telemetry and close if safe.
4) If not remediated: run targeted replay locally using rw-probe replay --id <probe-id> --limit 50 and attach traces to incident.
5) If regression confirmed, enact rollback via rw-deploy rollback --model <model-id> --to-version <stable> and notify Customer Success.
6) Create regression triage ticket with tags: probe-farm, suspect-regression, immediate-followup and assign to model owner.
postmortem_template:
When a probe detects a confirmed regression, use the following summary fields in the postmortem:
- Incident ID
- Probe ID and probe type
- First detection timestamp
- Detection latency
- Root cause summary
- Remediation action taken and time-to-remediation
- Customer impact (routes affected, users impacted)
- Action items and owners for prevention
- Lessons learned and probe tuning suggestions
faq:
Q: How do we avoid probe churn (too many false positives)?
A: Tune assertion thresholds conservatively, increase analyzer ensemble weighting, and add notebook-driven manual review for new probe types during a 2-week burn-in.
Q: Can the Probe Farm run against private deployments?
A: Yes—private deployments require an on-prem Probe Agent and a permissions token; see eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides for onboarding.
Q: How often should we refresh honeypot probes?
A: Quarterly for static datasets, monthly for high-change domains (code assistants, instruction-tuned instruction sets).
notes: This playbook should be reviewed each quarter or after any major serving runtime release. Integration tests for the Probe Farm are in the eval-harness CI suite (see eval-harness CI job: ci/probe-farm-integration).
